== Biography ==
'''Agnes Glasgow''' appears in the Findmypast transcript for the Walston baptism entry dated 17 Feb 1712, which names [[Glasgow-4175|James Glasgow]] as father.<ref name="FMP1" /> Because the entry records a baptism rather than a birth, her birth is placed before that date, and Walston is inferred from the baptism rather than independently recorded.

== Research Notes ==
The held baptism transcript supports the recorded child and named father; it does not establish a later-life identity.

This indexed marriage entry predates the 1712 baptism attributed to this profile and is retained as a record of a possibly different Agnes, not as an event of this child. A late adult baptism would require positive evidence before reopening that identity. The banns/marriage index records Agnes Glasgow and James Swan on 12 May 1666 at Kirknewton and East Calder.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 690/10 / 55; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. This entry is excluded from the current 1712 child account; a later baptism would need positive supporting evidence.

=== Father relationship review — 24 October 2026 ===

Agnes Glasgow appears in the Findmypast transcript for a Walston baptism entry dated 17 February 1712; the transcript explicitly names James Glasgow as her father. The existing public profile [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-4175 James Glasgow] is record-defined by this same child entry, so the relationship is assessed 95% confident. This profile account is not independent corroboration; the underlying Findmypast transcript remains the evidence and its original parish image has not been inspected. Agnes’s birth remains before the baptism date and Walston is inferred from the event. The earlier banns/marriage entries predate the 1712 baptism attributed to this profile and are retained as records of other possibly same-named women, not as events of this child. A late adult baptism would require positive evidence before reopening those identities. The existing WikiTree father relationship remains attached and its saved unmarked certainty field is unchanged. The underlying record image remains uninspected.
